note: Prepared from the unit title and the trade's usual practice. An instructor must read and correct it, and mark it Ready, before it is opened for an intake.

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What is customer (client) service in a salon or spa?
options: Only the way the cashier takes payment at the end of a visit
The full list of the services and prices shown on the salon's wall
All that staff do to meet clients' needs and make them feel valued
The time the salon opens and closes each day

questions.stem: Why is good client service important to a salon or spa?
options: Happy clients come back and tell others, so the business grows
It lets the salon charge whatever price it likes for each service
It means staff do not need any technical skills
It is only important for new clients, not regulars

questions.stem: Who is an "internal customer"?
options: A client who has a service inside a treatment room
A client who lives in the same parish as the salon
A supplier who brings the stock deliveries inside the building
A co-worker who needs your help or work to do their job

questions.stem: What do most clients expect when they visit a salon or spa?
options: A free service on every third visit, whatever they book
A clean place, polite staff, a safe service and fair prices
To be served before anyone else, even without a booking
To be allowed into the stock room to choose their own products

questions.stem: A regular client always books with the same nail technician, Odane. What does this most likely tell you?
options: She does not like any other staff member at all
She wants to pay less than other clients
She trusts his work and values the relationship
She is not allowed to see other technicians

questions.stem: What is the best way to show a client that you are listening to her?
options: Look at her, nod, and repeat back the main points
Keep working on your phone while she talks
Finish each of her sentences for her so that it saves time
Think about your own reply while she speaks

questions.stem: Which of these is a "closed" question?
options: How would you like your hair styled today?
What products do you use on your skin?
Why did you stop using that cream?
Is the water temperature comfortable?

questions.stem: When is a closed question most useful?
options: When you want the client to describe her full routine
When you need a quick yes or no, such as checking comfort
When you want to start a long, friendly conversation with the client
When the client does not speak at all

questions.stem: A therapist uses words such as "comedones" and "desquamation" with a client. What should she do instead?
options: Use plain words, such as blackheads and dead skin cells
Use even more trade words, so she sounds expert
Say nothing at all during the treatment
Write the words down for the client to look up at home

questions.stem: Which body language could make a client feel unwelcome?
options: A warm smile and steady, friendly eye contact
Nodding and leaning in a little while she speaks
Folded arms, a frown and looking at the clock
Turning to face her when she talks

questions.stem: What is "rapport" with a client?
options: A written report on the client's hair or skin
A discount for clients who come in at least once every month
A form the client signs before a chemical service
A friendly, trusting relationship between you and the client

questions.stem: Which topics are best avoided when chatting with a client?
options: Her plans for the weekend and her holidays
Politics, religion and other clients' private lives
Hair care tips that suit the hot season
How she would like her nails shaped and finished

questions.stem: A client books a facial and says she has an important wedding on Saturday. What should the therapist do?
options: Use a strong peel so her skin glows by Saturday
Tell her it is too late to do anything for her skin
Ask about her skin and plan a treatment that suits the timing
Do the same facial she does for every other client, without asking

questions.stem: How can you find out what a client really wants from her service?
options: Ask questions, listen, and check her record
Guess from the way she is dressed and how she speaks
Do what you think looks best without asking
Ask another client what she would choose

questions.stem: Which is an example of "going the extra mile" for a client?
options: Doing the service she booked, then leaving her to find her own way out
Giving her a free product without asking the manager
Letting her skip paying because she is a regular
Calling a taxi for an older client when it starts to rain

questions.stem: Which set of qualities helps a worker give good client service?
options: Speed, silence and avoiding eye contact
Patience, politeness and a positive attitude
Strong opinions, a loud voice and a lot of jokes
Shyness and keeping away from clients

questions.stem: Why must staff arrive on time for their shift?
options: So that they can leave early on any day that the salon is quiet
Because the owner likes to see who comes first
So clients are seen on time and co-workers are not overloaded
So they have time to do their own hair first

questions.stem: Why should a complaint be seen as useful to the salon?
options: It shows what to improve and is a chance to keep the client
It shows which clients should be banned from coming back again
It lets the salon raise the price
It means the client will never return, so it can be ignored

questions.stem: A client says her pedicure polish chipped after one day. What is the best first reply?
options: "That never happens with our polish. You must have done something."
"Polish always chips. There is nothing we can do."
"You will have to book and pay for a new pedicure."
"I'm sorry about that. Let me look at it and see how we can fix it."

questions.stem: Which order of steps is a good way to handle a complaint?
options: Argue, explain the salon's side, then ask the client to leave
Listen, apologise, find a solution, act on it and follow up
Apologise, give a full refund, then listen if there is time
Ignore it, wait to see if the client complains again, then act

questions.stem: Why should complaints be written in a complaints record?
options: So the client can be charged for the time spent on the complaint
So staff can show the record to other clients
So the manager can spot problems that happen again and fix them
Because the client will be asked to sign it every visit

questions.stem: A client becomes very angry and starts to swear at a stylist. What should the stylist do?
options: Stay calm, do not swear back, and get the supervisor
Swear back so the client knows how it feels
Carry on working on her hair and say nothing at all
Walk out of the salon to go home for the day

questions.stem: When should a client's complaint be passed to the supervisor?
options: Never, because you should solve every complaint yourself
Only if the client threatens to post about it online
Only at the end of the month, with all the others
When it is beyond what you are allowed or able to solve

questions.stem: Which is a good way to collect client feedback?
options: Asking clients to rate their stylist in front of her
Listening in to clients' private phone calls
A short comment card or survey after the service
Guessing from how much each client tips

questions.stem: A client posts a poor review of the spa online. What is the best response?
options: Reply with an angry post that names the client and her faults
Reply politely, apologise and invite her to get in touch
Ask friends to post lots of good reviews to hide it
Ignore it, as online reviews never matter to a business

questions.stem: What should the salon do with the feedback it collects?
options: Read it, share it with staff and use it to improve the service
File it away in a box without anyone reading it at all
Keep only the good comments and throw the rest away
Post all of it on the salon's wall, with the clients' names on it

questions.stem: What are "service standards" in a salon?
options: The prices that the government sets for each service in a salon
The hours each stylist must work each week
The brands of products the salon must use
The salon's rules for how every client is looked after

questions.stem: Why does teamwork matter for good client service?
options: It means one person can do all the work while the others have a rest
It lets staff blame each other when something goes wrong
Staff help each other so clients get a smooth, on-time service
It means clients must be served by more than one person

questions.stem: A co-worker is busy, and her waiting client would like a drink of water. You are free. What should you do?
options: Leave it, because it is not your client
Get the client a drink and let your co-worker know
Tell the client to get her own water
Wait and see if anyone else in the salon does it first

questions.stem: Why should staff treat every client with equal respect, whatever her age, race, religion or disability?
options: Everyone deserves fair treatment, and it is the right thing to do
Because clients who are different will pay more for services
So staff can choose which clients they like and serve them first
Only because the law says so, not for any other reason

questions.stem: A client asks for a style that is important to her religion or culture. What should the stylist do?
options: Tell her a different style would suit her better
Laugh and say the style is old-fashioned
Do the style she wants but make jokes about it
Respect her wishes and ask questions to get it right

questions.stem: A client asks a nail technician to do a service she is not trained for. What should the technician do?
options: Try it anyway, as the client will not know
Do it quickly and charge less, just in case it goes wrong
Explain honestly and find a trained co-worker or another time
Watch a short video on her phone first and then go ahead with it

questions.stem: Why must a therapist not promise results she cannot be sure of, such as "no more spots"?
options: It makes the treatment take longer
It is dishonest and the client will be let down
It means the client must pay for the treatment in advance
It is only allowed for products, not services

questions.stem: Why is checking for contraindications (reasons not to treat) part of good client service?
options: It keeps the client safe, which matters more than a sale
It lets staff charge an extra fee for the check
It is only needed if the client asks for it
It gives staff a reason to turn away clients they find difficult

questions.stem: During a facial, a client says the mask is burning her skin. What should the therapist do?
options: Tell her this is normal and leave it on for the full time
Add more of the mask so it works faster
Leave the room so the client can relax
Remove it at once with cool water and check the skin

questions.stem: Why might a salon contact a client a few days after a new chemical service, if she agreed to this?
options: To ask her to pay again for the service
To sell her contact details on to other businesses in the area
To check she is happy and answer her aftercare questions
To remind her that the stylist was very busy that day

questions.stem: Which of these helps build client loyalty?
options: Remembering her preferences and rewarding regular visits
Changing her stylist at every visit without telling her why
Raising prices for regular clients only
Keeping her waiting so she knows the salon is busy

questions.stem: Why is aftercare advice part of good client service?
options: It gives the stylist something to talk about while the client pays
It helps the client keep the result and avoid problems at home
It makes sure the client buys every product in the salon
It stops the client from coming back too soon

questions.stem: Why should staff avoid strong perfume when working close to clients?
options: It makes the salon's products smell weaker
Perfume is too costly for staff to wear at work
Clients will keep asking where they can buy the same perfume
It can upset clients with allergies, asthma or headaches

questions.stem: How can a therapist protect a client's privacy and dignity during a body treatment?
options: Leave the treatment room door open so others can see in
Ask her to undress fully while the therapist stays in the room and watches
Keep her covered with towels except the area being worked on
Talk about her body shape to other staff afterwards

questions.stem: A client wants a long chat while other clients are waiting. What should the stylist do?
options: Stay friendly but politely keep the service moving on time
Stop working and keep chatting for as long as she likes to talk
Tell her rudely to stop talking
Ignore her and play music loudly

questions.stem: A stylist is having a bad day at home. How should this affect her clients?
options: She should tell each client about it so they understand
It should not: she keeps her problems away from clients
She can be short with clients, as they will understand
She should rush her clients so she can go home early

questions.stem: A client sends the salon a message on social media asking about prices. What should staff do?
options: Ignore it, as only phone calls should be answered
Reply with prices from last year that may be out of date
Post her question and name publicly to answer everyone
Reply politely and soon, with the correct information

questions.stem: A stylist's mistake made a client late for work. After apologising, what else might the salon do, with the manager's agreement?
options: Blame the client for booking too close to work
Charge her extra for the time she was in the chair
Offer a gesture, such as a free treatment next time
Ask her to sign a form saying it will not happen again

questions.stem: Why should a client's preferences, such as her favourite drink or how she likes her nails, be noted on her record?
options: So the salon can charge her more next time for each special request
So any staff member can give her the same personal service next time
So the details can be shared on social media
So staff can talk about her habits with other clients

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: Clients who come in from outside the business to buy services are called what kind of customers?
What do we call the opinion a client forms in the first few seconds of meeting you?
What do we call the way your voice sounds, such as warm, cold or angry, which shows your feelings?
What word means understanding and sharing how another person feels?
What is the word for treating a person unfairly because of their race, religion, age or disability?
What word describes always being on time for work and for clients' appointments?
What word means keeping a client's personal details private?
What word is used for the standards of right and wrong behaviour that guide a professional at work?
Happy clients tell their friends about a good salon. What is this kind of free advertising called?
What is the card called that is stamped at each visit and gives the client a reward after a set number of visits?
What two words describe the steps a business takes to put things right and win back a client after a mistake?
Four clients give a spa scores of 4, 5, 3 and 4 out of 5. What is the average score?
What word describes how pleased a client is that the service met her needs?
What do we call a client who comes in for a service without an appointment?
Which senior person should a stylist call when a complaint is more than she is allowed to solve?

essays.stem: Explain what quality client service means in a salon or spa, and why it matters to the client, the staff and the business.
essays.modelAnswer: Quality client service means meeting each client's needs in a way that makes her feel welcome, safe and valued, from the first phone call to the follow-up after her visit. It includes a clean, comfortable salon, polite and well-groomed staff, a careful consultation, a safe and skilled service, honest advice and a fair bill. It matters to the client because she gets the result she wanted, feels respected and enjoys her visit. It matters to the staff because happy clients are easier to work with, ask for them again and may tip, and the job is more satisfying. It matters to the business because most of a salon's income comes from regular clients. Clients who are well served come back, buy products and tell their friends, which brings new clients at no cost. Poor service loses clients and gives the salon a bad name.
markingPoints: Defines quality service: meeting needs so the client feels welcome, safe and valued
Gives examples across the visit (welcome, consultation, safe service, honest advice)
Explains the benefit to the client
Explains the benefit to the staff
Explains the benefit to the business: repeat clients, sales and word of mouth

essays.stem: Describe how a stylist or therapist finds out and meets a client's needs and expectations during a consultation.
essays.modelAnswer: The consultation starts before any service begins, with the client seated comfortably and the worker facing her. The worker checks the client's record for past services, allergies and notes. She asks open questions such as "What would you like done today?" and "How do you care for your hair at home?", and closed questions to check facts. She looks at, and where suitable feels, the hair, skin or nails, and checks for any contraindications. She looks at any photos the client shows, and talks about what is possible, how long it will take and what it will cost, so the client's expectations are realistic. If something cannot be done safely or well, she explains why and suggests another choice. She repeats the plan back and gets the client's agreement before starting. During the service she checks that the client is comfortable and happy, and records what was done.
markingPoints: Checks the client record for past services and allergies
Uses open and closed questions and listens
Looks at the hair, skin or nails and checks for contraindications
Agrees a realistic result, time and cost, and explains any limits
Gets agreement before starting, checks comfort during, and records the service

essays.stem: Explain how good questioning and listening skills help you serve clients well. Give an example of an open question and a closed question, and say when you would use each.
essays.modelAnswer: Questioning and listening help me find out what the client really wants, so I do not guess and make mistakes. Good listening means I give the client my full attention, look at her, nod, do not interrupt, and repeat the main points back, for example "So you want to keep the length but take off the dry ends." This shows I care and lets her correct me if I have it wrong. An open question lets the client answer in her own words and gives me more detail. An example is "How would you like your nails to look today?" I use open questions at the start of a consultation to learn her wishes and routine. A closed question can be answered with yes or no, such as "Is the water too hot?" or "Have you had a skin test for this tint?" I use closed questions to check facts and comfort quickly during a service.
markingPoints: Explains that questioning and listening find the client's true needs and avoid mistakes
Describes active listening: attention, eye contact, no interrupting, repeating back
Gives a correct example of an open question
Gives a correct example of a closed question
Says when each is used: open to explore, closed to check facts and comfort

essays.stem: A client comes back two days after a hair colour and says the shade is much darker than she wanted. Describe the steps you would take to deal with her complaint.
essays.modelAnswer: I would greet her politely and take her to a quiet area, so she can talk freely and other clients are not upset. I would listen to the whole complaint without interrupting, and look at her hair in good light. I would apologise that she is not happy, without arguing or blaming anyone. I would check her record to see the colour, the developer and the timing used, and repeat back what she has told me so we agree on the problem. Then I would explain the possible solutions, for example a colour correction or a lighter gloss, done by a senior stylist, and I would call the supervisor, who must agree to any free service or refund. When a solution is agreed, I would book it as soon as she can come. I would record the complaint and what was done, and later call her, if she agrees, to check she is happy.
markingPoints: Moves to a quiet area and listens fully without interrupting
Apologises without arguing or blaming
Checks the facts: looks at the hair and checks the colour record
Offers solutions with the supervisor's agreement and books the correction
Records the complaint and follows up with the client

essays.stem: Describe ways a salon or spa can collect feedback from clients, and explain how it should use that feedback.
essays.modelAnswer: A salon can collect feedback in several ways. Staff can ask clients at the end of the visit how they found the service, and listen to the answer. A short comment card or survey can be given at the desk, with a few questions and a space for comments, and a box where it can be left without a name. The salon can send a short message or online survey after the visit to clients who agreed to be contacted. It can also read the reviews and comments on its social media pages and review sites. To use the feedback, the manager should read it all, the good and the bad, and look for comments that come up again and again. Good comments should be shared with staff to praise them. Problems should be discussed at a staff meeting and an action agreed, such as shorter waiting times. The salon should check later whether the change worked.
markingPoints: Asking clients in person at the end of the visit
Comment cards or short surveys, which can be anonymous
Messages or online surveys to clients who agreed, and reading online reviews
Reads all feedback and looks for repeated points
Shares praise, agrees actions on problems and checks the change worked

essays.stem: Clients come from many backgrounds and have different needs. Explain how staff can give fair, respectful service to every client.
essays.modelAnswer: Staff should treat every client with the same respect and care, whatever her age, race, religion, culture, gender, size, disability or how much money she has. They should never make jokes or comments about a client's background or body. They should listen to what each client wants and not assume, for example by asking how she wears her hair for her faith or culture. Staff should learn to work with all hair and skin types that come into a Jamaican salon or spa, and suggest products that suit them. For clients with a disability, they should ask what help is wanted, keep the way clear, and allow extra time if needed. For a client who does not speak English well, they should speak simply and use pictures or writing. Staff must also follow the salon's rules on fair treatment. Fair service makes every client feel welcome and is the right thing to do.
markingPoints: Treats every client with equal respect, whatever her background
Avoids jokes, comments or assumptions about a client's background or body
Asks about and respects cultural or religious wishes
Adapts for disability or language needs: asks what help is wanted, allows time, speaks simply
Explains that fair service is right and makes every client feel welcome

essays.stem: Explain how good teamwork between staff, including help for internal customers, improves the service clients receive. Give examples.
essays.modelAnswer: An internal customer is a co-worker who needs your help or your work to do their own job. Good teamwork means staff help each other so that the client gets a smooth, on-time service. For example, the receptionist books the right amount of time and passes on messages quickly, so the stylist is ready when the client arrives. A junior who shampoos clients well and on time helps the stylist keep to her bookings. If a therapist is running late, a free co-worker can greet her next client, offer a drink and explain the delay. Staff who keep the stock room tidy and report low stock help everyone find what they need. Good teamwork also means sharing information, such as a client's allergy, and never arguing in front of clients. When staff work together, clients wait less, feel looked after, and see a happy, professional team.
markingPoints: Explains what an internal customer is
Gives a reception or booking example
Gives an example of helping a co-worker with her client
Mentions sharing information and not arguing in front of clients
Explains the result for clients: less waiting and a smooth, professional service

essays.stem: Explain how a salon or spa can build client loyalty so that clients keep coming back.
essays.modelAnswer: Loyalty starts with a good, safe service every time, so the client trusts the results. Staff should greet clients by name and remember their preferences, such as the stylist they like, the drink they take or how they like their nails shaped, and note these on the record so any staff member can give the same personal service. Good consultations and honest advice show the client that staff care about her, not just the sale. Clear aftercare advice helps her keep the result, which makes her happy with the salon. The salon can reward regular clients with a loyalty card, a birthday treat or offers for those who rebook. Rebooking the next appointment before she leaves helps her keep coming. Following up after new services, and dealing quickly and kindly with any complaint, show that the salon values her. Clients who feel valued stay loyal.
markingPoints: Gives a good, safe service every time
Uses the client's name and records and remembers her preferences
Gives honest advice and clear aftercare
Rewards regular clients and rebooks before they leave
Follows up and deals well with complaints

essays.stem: Explain what professional and ethical behaviour means for a salon or spa worker. Give at least four examples.
essays.modelAnswer: Professional and ethical behaviour means doing the right thing for clients, co-workers and the business, even when no one is watching. First, the worker is honest: she does not make false claims about results, and she charges the correct prices. Second, she works only within her training and skills; if a client asks for a service she cannot do safely, she says so and refers her to a trained co-worker. Third, she keeps client information confidential and does not gossip about clients or co-workers. Fourth, she puts the client's safety first: she checks for contraindications, does skin tests as the maker requires, and refers a client to a doctor when needed, even if it means losing a sale. Fifth, she follows hygiene rules and uses single-use items once only. She is also punctual, well groomed and polite. This behaviour builds trust and protects clients and the salon's good name.
markingPoints: Defines it as doing what is right for clients, co-workers and the business
Honesty: no false claims and correct prices
Works within her skills and refers when needed
Keeps information confidential and does not gossip
Puts safety and hygiene first (contraindications, skin tests, single-use items)

essays.stem: Explain how a stylist or therapist keeps a client safe and comfortable during a service, and why this is part of quality client service.
essays.modelAnswer: Before the service, the worker checks the client's record and asks about allergies, medical conditions and medicines, and looks for contraindications such as cuts, infections or recent sunburn. If any are found, she does not treat and advises the client to see a doctor. She makes sure any skin test the maker requires has been done. She uses clean, disinfected tools, fresh towels and single-use items for each client. She tests the heat of water, wax or tools on her own inner wrist before they touch the client. She protects the client's clothes with a gown, and her privacy and dignity with towels and closed doors. During the service she asks if the client is comfortable, checks the water temperature and the pressure, and stops at once if there is pain or burning. Safety and comfort are part of quality service because a client who is hurt or uncomfortable will not trust the salon or return.
markingPoints: Checks the record and contraindications, and refers to a doctor if needed
Makes sure required skin tests are done
Uses clean, disinfected tools, fresh towels and single-use items
Tests heat on her inner wrist, protects privacy, and checks comfort during the service
Explains that safety and comfort build trust and bring the client back

practical1.title: Handle client complaints in role plays and complete the complaint records
practical1.brief: As a group, practise dealing with client complaints in the Centre's salon or spa. The assessor gives each member a complaint card, for example: a hair colour darker than the client wanted; nail polish that chipped after one day; a client kept waiting 40 minutes; a client who says her facial made her skin red; a client who was charged the wrong price; a client unhappy with a rude remark. Take turns so that every member handles one complaint as the staff member, while others play the client and the supervisor, and one member keeps notes and another takes the photos. For each complaint, the staff member moves the client to a quiet area, listens without interrupting, apologises, checks the facts, agrees a solution within her authority or calls the supervisor, and thanks the client. She then fills in a complaint record form. At the end, the group meets and writes a short action list: one change the salon could make for each complaint so it does not happen again. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Photos show people from behind or hands and papers, not faces, unless the person agrees and the Centre allows it. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: The Centre's price list and a sample appointment page
Chart paper and markers for the action list
Pens and a clipboard for the note-taker
photos: The quiet area set up for the role plays
Each member listening to the client during a role play (from behind or the side)
The supervisor being called in for a complaint that needs it
Each member's completed complaint record form
The note-taker's notes for each role play
checklist: Moved the client to a quiet area and stayed calm and polite
Listened to the whole complaint without interrupting, using open body language
Apologised sincerely without arguing or blaming
Checked the facts and repeated the problem back to the client
Offered a fair solution within their authority, or called the supervisor
Thanked the client and explained what would happen next
Filled in the complaint record form clearly and completely
Suggested a sensible change for the group's action list
safety: Use made-up client names and details only
Keep role plays calm: no shouting or touching, even when acting angry
Keep the area tidy, with chairs and bags out of walkways
Stop any role play that upsets a member, and tell the assessor

practical2.title: Design and run a client feedback survey, and present an improvement plan
practical2.brief: As a group, find out what clients think of the service in the Centre's salon or spa, and suggest improvements. First, together, design a short feedback card of five to eight questions, using a 1 to 5 score and one open question, on topics such as the welcome, waiting time, cleanliness, the service, advice and value. Then each member collects feedback from at least three people: trainees, staff or Centre clients who agree to take part, without writing their names. Together, add up the scores for each question, work out the average score, and draw a simple bar chart. Pick the three lowest scores, and plan one improvement for each: what will change, who will do it and by when. Show the results and the plan on an A3 poster. Each member presents one part of the poster to the assessor: the card, the results, the chart, or one improvement. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: Paper or card for the feedback cards, and a box to collect them
Pens, a calculator and a ruler
A3 card or chart paper and markers
The Centre's service standards or customer charter, if there is one
photos: The draft feedback card with the group's changes
The finished feedback cards ready to hand out
The tally of scores and the averages worked out
The finished poster with the improvement plan
Each member presenting their part of the poster
checklist: Helped write clear, polite questions in plain words
Asked people politely and explained what the survey was for
Kept the feedback anonymous and did not argue with any answer
Added up scores and worked out averages correctly
Drew or helped draw an accurate bar chart
Suggested a practical improvement with who and when
Presented their part clearly and answered a question about it
safety: Ask people only if they agree to take part, and keep the cards anonymous
Do not enter treatment rooms during a service to collect feedback
Use markers in a ventilated room and put the caps back on
Keep walkways clear while working on the poster
